title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An Avride autonomous vehicle in Austin struck and killed a duck in a neighborhood lake area without slowing or stopping. The vehicle was operating in autonomous mode when the incident occurred. This shows a perception or decision-making failure in which the system did not recognize a slow-moving animal in its path or did not classify it as an obstacle requiring evasion or braking.

A resident also alleged the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this after reviewing its data and simulations. It is not established whether the vehicle actually violated that traffic control requirement. The incident occurred in a deployed testing operation, not a controlled environment, meaning the system encountered real-world conditions including pedestrians and animals it had to handle without human intervention in that moment.

The failure would have been caught by either a human safety driver capable of overriding autonomous control, or by perception systems tested against the full range of obstacles in the areas where testing was permitted. In response, Avride restricted operations on certain streets and began evaluating technological improvements, suggesting the existing system did not reliably handle the circumstances it encountered.

summary:
# Summary

An Avride autonomous vehicle operating in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, prompting significant community backlash. The duck, which residents recognized because it was nesting outside a local restaurant, was hit by the self-driving car without the vehicle slowing down or stopping. A neighborhood resident also alleged the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data and simulation replays.

In response to the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode at the time and has restricted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake. The company is now evaluating technological improvements to prevent similar situations, including running controlled experiments in simulation to ensure safety performance remains unaffected. Local residents saved the duck's eggs by placing them in an incubator. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, also operate in Austin.
